title: Sourcing & Legal Clarity - Stakeholder Mapping
summary: Intro to procurement and legal requirements for Redwood inference pilot. Discussed MSA/DPA redlines, SLA floors, KMS and egress, pilot scope and metrics, pricing workbook ask, and next steps to share docs and schedule redline review.
action_items: Owner: Jordan Patel; Item: Share latest MSA + DPA baseline and example redline tracker; Due: 2025-10-24
Owner: Elena Morris; Item: Flag legal must-haves (data residency, audit log retention, breach notification SLA) and return comments; Due: 2025-10-28
Owner: Maya Liu; Item: Prepare short tech runbook for VPC-private pilot including expected network ports and egress estimate; Due: 2025-10-22

SE-led pilot scoping workshop week of 10/20 (Maya to lead)
Agree on SLA floor & pilot acceptance criteria before pilot kickoff
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-17
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Carlos Reyes (Redwood CSM), Samir Khan (Evergreen - Procurement), Elena Morris (Evergreen - Legal), Priya Desai (Evergreen - Eng Mgr), Tom Fletcher (Evergreen - FinOps)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): ok hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, I see most folks, I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, my SE Maya and Carlos from success are here. quick round robin?
[00:18] Samir (Procurement): Samir here, head of procurement, want to get this through sourcing gate in Q4 so timeline is tight.
[00:27] Elena (Legal): Elena, legal counsel. we'll focus on MSA/DPA and a couple of non-negotiables for us.
[00:33] Priya (Eng): Priya, engineering manager - want to understand the private deployment options and perf expectations.
[00:40] Tom (FinOps): Tom - I'll own the pricing inputs and cost model.
[00:44] Maya (Redwood SE): hi all, I'll be running the pilot scoping and tech fit.

[02:05] Jordan: high level — Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. For procurement reasons i want to flag that customer had asked for a VPC private option earlier? (murmur) right Samir?
[02:32] Samir: correct, due to data classification we'd prefer private VPC or dedicated at minimum. hosted is okay for non-sensitive flows but main workloads need isolated tenancy.
[02:48] Elena: legal: we need data residency guarantees, audit logs for seven years, and breach notif within 72 hours. SOC2 plus an attestation is table stakes. also key custody - KMS or HSM integration required.
[03:12] Jordan: got it. we support customer-managed KMS via Redwood Private and Dedicated — Maya will walk through options. quick question on SLA floor — what's the acceptable uptime and latency envelope for you?
[03:30] Tom: finops wants an SLA we can measure against. Uptime 99.9 minimum for the customer-facing flows, and p95 latency under 300ms for single-turn generation if possible. If dedicated or private that helps.
[03:50] Maya: couple clarifications — p95 300ms depends on model and sequence length, we can pick a quantized model profile to hit that. also batching impacts per-token cost, so there's a tradeoff.

[05:10] Jordan: on contracts — typical path is MSA + DPA; we can provide Redwood's standard MSA and a DPA with data processing addendum. Elena, are there any redlines that typically block intake?
[05:27] Elena: main blockers are indemnity carve outs, subprocessor list and 3rd party transfers, and data deletion obligations on termination. Also egress fees need to be explicit; we can't have surprise transfer charges.
[05:48] Jordan: we can show the subprocessor roster; egress fees are in the pricing workbook but we'll call them out. Tom, you will fill those expected volumes?
[05:58] Tom: yes I'll populate the workbook. quick ask though — any minimum commit would change pricing materially, we prefer pay-as-you-go but can discuss a small pilot commit.

[07:20] Samir: procurement wants a clear billing path and a billing contact; also escrow/escrow alternatives for source? Some finance people asked if there's an escrow for the runtime — is that a thing?
[07:32] Jordan: we do have an escrow conversation for enterprise but it's not default. we can raise it with legal channel if needed.

[08:00] Maya: techfit — two main onboarding models: (1) Redwood Hosted API with VPC peering and private endpoints, (2) Redwood Private where control plane runs in our tenancy but data plane sits in customer VPC or on-prem. For regulated workloads option 2 is preferred.
[08:30] Priya: if we go private, what's the expected ops overhead? we have a small infra team.
[08:40] Maya: we provide a managed package; you'll see about 1-2 hours/week of runbook ops initially for tuning, after that it's low. we do need network team to open ports and manage routing.

[10:12] Jordan: on security attestations — SOC2 type II report is available, we can share. we also support SAML/SSO and RBAC. Elena: would you accept RBAC + audit logs for separation of duties?
[10:30] Elena: yes, but need proof of log retention and tamper evidence, so WORM-like retention for audit logs would be preferred.

[11:45] Maya: noted. KMS options: customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or GCP KMS, or HSM using our integration. key access logs are available via CloudTrail. Sometimes transcripts mis-annotate KV cache as K V cash in our docs so just flagging that term.

[13:05] Tom: egress math — can you give a ballpark on egress per 1M tokens?
[13:12] Maya: egress depends on response size, but rough estimate: 1M tokens of small responses ~ 200GB. egress fee at retail cloud rate; we'll put a model in the workbook.

[15:00] Jordan: let's talk timelines — procurement wants sourcing decision by end of October. Pilot ideally starts in November. Is that realistic?
[15:12] Samir: yes, but we need legal signoff first. Elena: we need a redline review and a vanilla MSA isn't sufficient.

[15:45] Maya: for pilot scope — SE suggests a 4-week pilot: week 0 infra prep, week 1 ingestion and integration with our SDK, weeks 2-3 load & perf, week 4 evaluation and acceptance. Acceptance criteria: p95 latency target, inference correctness on a small eval set, and error rate below 1%.

[17:30] Priya: acceptance criteria sounds good. we also want a regression check against current heuristic system to ensure parity on quality.

[18:50] Elena: on DPA — we need subprocessors enumerated and a clause for audits and right to audit for regulated data. Also clarify retention limits and deletion mechanics. If Redwood offers private deployment the data residency piece is easier.

[20:10] Jordan: we can offer to run the private pilot in your preferred region for residency. we'll include that in the MSA/DPA pipeline.

[21:45] Tom: about pricing — are there pilot credits? sometimes vendors offer credits for the pilot phase to offset egress and initial tuning costs.
[22:00] Carlos (CSM): we often provide pilot credits on a case-by-case basis; Jordan will confirm.

[23:20] Jordan: ok i'll confirm credits; for pricing path we have pay-as-you-go rates and reserved capacity discounts. if you commit to a small monthly reserved capacity for pilot we can lower egress or token rates.

[25:05] Samir: procurement will need to know SLA remediation and service credits in the MSA. can you accept a 10% monthly credit for SLA breach beyond 99.9?
[25:20] Jordan: our standard SLA tiers include credits, we can propose 10% for sustained downtime beyond agreed SLOs — Maya will pull the SLA language.

[26:50] Maya: quick note on fallbacks — we support model fallbacks and auto-rollbacks if a new model fails QA. for production workloads we recommend canaries and a traffic split.

[28:05] Elena: we will ask for a clause that protects PII and a definition of PII in the DPA. Also, incident response timeline: 72 hours for notification and 30 days for incident report.

[29:10] Jordan: understood. we'll mark those as legal must-haves.

[30:00] Priya: connectivity — is there support for private peering?
[30:06] Maya: yes, private peering or VPN with BGP is supported; we'll provide the network checklist.

[31:30] Tom: on cost modeling — if reserved capacity reduces per-token cost by 30% is that typical?
[31:40] Jordan: depends on model family and quantization; reserved can be 20-40% savings. we'll give a sample rate card.

[33:10] Samir: procurement will also want a clean termination clause and exit assistance — data export, deletion certs.
[33:22] Elena: yes, and we need to know data return timelines.

[34:05] Jordan: we provide export tooling and deletion certs; we'll add timelines to the DPA (typically 30-45 days).

[35:40] Maya: technical deep-dive items to call out for the redline: network ports, service accounts, expected hostnames, and KV cache persistence semantics. some docs refer to KV cache TTLs which can confuse SREs.

[37:05] Priya: we'll need a short impact analysis on how inference latency will affect our app — Maya can run a short benchmark.

[37:30] Maya: yes I can run a targeted benchmark — need an example payload and the sequence length distribution.

[38:10] Tom: i'll send token volume profiles and peak qps in the workbook.

[39:00] Jordan: on legal timeline — Elena when can you turn around initial redlines if we send the MSA today?
[39:08] Elena: typically 5-7 business days for initial redlines, but if we prioritize maybe 3. depends on backlog.

[40:20] Jordan: great. we'll aim to get the docs to you today. Carlos will be copied for onboarding.

[41:50] Samir: procurement question — are there any export controls or restricted model policies?
[41:58] Maya: we follow sanctions lists and restrict families where required; we can provide export control doc.

[42:45] Elena: also curious if Redwood will accept a one-way NDA for some of our internal eval data.

[43:00] Jordan: yes NDA is fine, we'll coordinate with legal.

[44:15] Priya: quick tech q — support for function calling / tooling? we want to call internal tools with structured outputs.

[44:25] Maya: yes we support structured output and tool-calling; will show integration patterns in the SE workshop.

[45:50] Tom: can you share the pricing_workbook_v2 link right now?
[45:55] Jordan: yes attaching in chat — Shared doc: pricing_workbook_v2 (link) and MSA_DPA_baseline_v3 (link).

[47:20] Carlos: we've also got a short onboarding checklist and pilot runbook I'll share after.

[48:05] Jordan: ok to recap — Jordan will send MSA/DPA baseline + pricing workbook and confirm pilot credit ask. Maya to schedule pilot scoping workshop w/ Priya for week of 10/20. Elena will return legal redlines by 10/28 (target). Tom to fill workbook with volumes by 10/21.

[49:10] Elena: yes that's right. One more ask: can we get a SOC2 attestation and a list of subprocessors?
[49:22] Jordan: yes we'll share SOC2 + subprocessor list.

[50:00] Samir: sounds good. procurement will queue the sourcing doc once legal thumbs up.

[50:20] Jordan: thanks everyone for the time; we'll follow up with the items and the redline session invite.
[50:30] Priya: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[50:35] Tom: thanks, bye.
[50:40] Maya: bye.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts referenced: pricing_workbook_v2 (link to drive), MSA_DPA_baseline_v3 (link to drive), onboarding_runbook_draft.pdf (link).

Notes on transcription: speakers labelled by role; occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"), some punctuation flattened.
